subject: Fuaran-Core
$comment: Phase 203. `proofs/README.md` says this repository is "exhaustively proved in the sense a parametric spine admits", and until this file that sentence was prose: nothing computed it, so every survey found another packable package with no model and no record of whether it needed one, and filed a phase. The stopping rule is that COVERAGE IS TOTAL OR DECLARED — every packable package (the derived roster Phase 199 asserts) is either named by a model in `modules.json` or has an entry here. There is no third state, and a package in neither fails the `Proofs.Coverage` family. An entry is a RECORDED DECISION, not an excuse: it names the package, the closed reason, and enough prose for a later operator to disagree with it. Deleting an entry is how that operator asks for a theorem — the gate then names the gap on the next run and keeps naming it until a model exists. The check runs BOTH WAYS, on the `fable-exclusions.json` precedent (Phase 185; at `tests/fable-smoke/exclusions.json` until Phase 217): an entry naming a package that is no longer packable, or one that has SINCE GAINED a model, fails too, because a reason that outlives the fact it describes is how the comment Phase 185 replaced came to say something untrue. Hand-authored; the reason vocabulary below is closed and every term in it is carried by at least one entry, so no term is a vocabulary nothing tests.

reasons.facade: The package is a surface over packages that ARE modelled and adds no semantics of its own — what a theorem here would state is its callee's theorem, restated in a second syntax. A defect in a facade is a mapping defect, which is what the certification tests it carries are for.
reasons.law-tested-by-design: The package HAS concrete computation and the theorem has been declined in favour of a shipped `Conformance` law family, which the entry NAMES. That is a weaker claim than a proof and the entry says so: a law is sampled at a witness, a theorem is not. The named family must exist in the shipped law-family roster (`Fuaran.Core.Families`, Phase 184), so an entry cannot cite a law no census enumerates.
reasons.content-free-seam: The package is a generic seam whose content is supplied entirely by the domain — Core owns no concrete computation here to state a theorem ABOUT. What it can promise is the shape of the seam, and that is stated where a domain meets it rather than as a theorem over a model of nothing.

$reasonsNotCarried: Phase 203 was filed naming four reasons and carries three. `tooling` (a build-time tool whose contract is the shape of what it emits) was written for `Fuaran.Core.Idl.Codegen`'s emitter, and by the time this file was cut that package HAD a model: the six generated-vocabulary modules are its F* target's own output, and `check.ps1`'s header says in as many words that what the leg proves over them is the F* BACKEND. A `tooling` entry for it would have been stale on arrival, which is exactly what this file's second direction fails. `leaving-core` was written for a `Lease` package that had already left. A closed vocabulary term with no entry is a term nothing tests — so both were dropped rather than carried, and `content-free-seam` was added for the three packages whose content is the domain's. The reasoning is recorded in `README.md` under "Coverage is total or declared".

exclusions.note: The profile-pinned `Digest` constructor (DECISIONS.md D122, route B): `ofValue` is `Canonical.tryWrite` under the named profile, hashed by `Fuaran.Core.Tree`'s SHA-256, and `ofCanonicalText` admits stored text only where `Canonical.isCanonical` holds. It adds no semantics of its own — the rendering is `Wire`'s (the `WireCanon` model and the profile vectors), the digest `Tree`'s (the known-answer and platform-parity pins) — so a theorem here would restate its two callees'. What it owns, that the digest is of exactly the canonical bytes under both profiles and that every stored result hash in the apply corpus reproduces through it, is pinned by `CodecTests`.

A dotnet tool (`OutputType` Exe, `PackAsTool`, command `fuaran-core-idl`): argv parsing and file I/O over `Fuaran.Core.Idl.Codegen`'s generation half, which carries the six generated-vocabulary models. Nothing it computes survives a theorem that is not its callee's; what it owns — which switch reaches which backend — is checked by the codegen test families.

The law kit itself. Every family it exports is stated over an ABSTRACT witness the domain supplies, so there is no concrete computation here for a theorem to be about — a model of `footprintLaws` would be a model of the statement of an obligation. What can be checked about the kit is that its roster is complete and that every family runs under `certify` or sits on a declared opt-out, and Phase 194 and `ConformanceFamiliesTests` do exactly that. The one thing this entry must not be read as saying is that the laws are unchecked: they are, by the census, at every consumer's own witness.

The generic BUILD-TIME rule framework: `RuleFamily` + `Registry` + `PackRule`, with every rule's content supplied by a domain pack. `Validator.runAll` walks a pure registry and aggregates what the domain's own rules return, so a theorem here would prove that a fold over a list is a fold over a list. The one strand in this package with content of its own — `ColumnValidator` — is certified by `Conformance.columnarValidatorLaws`, over a seed-replayable sample with injected faults.

The RUNTIME analogue of the validator framework, and content-free for the same reason it states about itself: Core owns no flag vocabulary and no input shape, so register/snapshot/derive/subscribe is plumbing around a pure derivation the domain writes. A verification pack is the monetizable unit precisely BECAUSE the content is not here. It carries no `Conformance` family today, which this entry states rather than hides — an operator who wants the seam's own promises certified deletes this entry and the gate names the gap.

The read-token-lever seam. It has real computation — `Projection.project` / `render` / `parseBack` — and the family certifies the round trip, the digest's stability under presentation moves, and the compactness floor, at a domain's own `ProjectionWitness` with `wireEncode` and `applyOps` as per-call parameters. The theorem is declined rather than impossible: what it would take is a model of a domain codec this repository deliberately does not depend on, which is the same boundary the family's own parameters draw.

The proposal surface — pattern bank, proposals, decide/submit plumbing. The family runs the domain's own `Decide` (Phase 246) and is starved unless that policy allows, parks and denies something the generator draws; `Conformance.aiSurfaceLawsUnderKitPolicy` is the variant that swaps in the kit's policy to certify the plumbing for any policy. The one part of this strand that IS proved is arbitration, and it is proved where it lives: `Arbitration` ships in `Fuaran.Core.Ops` and carries `proofs/Arbitrate.fst` — which is why this entry is about the surface and not about the algorithm behind it.

$retired: Phase 154 RETIRED the `Fuaran.Core.DataFrame` entry (`law-tested-by-design`, citing `Conformance.incrementalLaws`, filed by Phase 203): the package has a model now — `proofs/Pipeline.fst`, the counted pipeline driver over an abstract step evaluator — and clause 1's second direction fails an exclusion for a package that has since gained one. What that entry declined is still declined and is still a recorded decision, only now it is the model's own: the fourteen verb SEMANTICS are the step evaluator, a parameter, and stay with the laws the entry named (`incrementalLaws`, `schemaWalkLaws`, `aggregateParityLaws`) rather than with a theorem — see `pipeline-step-evaluator-abstract` in `../proofs.json` and theorem 14 in `README.md`. The supersession of D14's reading for this package is `DECISIONS.md` D57 (operator decision 2026-09-25), which is where the decision lives; an operator who wants a verb proved reads that row and that entry, not this file. Phase 258 moved the package itself, with `proofs/Pipeline.fst`, `proofs/ColumnOps.fst`, their `proofs.json` rows and the two Phase 257 exclusions (`Fuaran.Core.DataFrame.CSharp`, `Fuaran.Core.DataFrame.Conformance`), to https://github.com/Fuaran-Core/fuaran-core-compute (DECISIONS.md D66); the rows and theorems this note cites are that repository's now. Phase 306 RETIRED the `Fuaran.Core.Column` entry (`law-tested-by-design`, citing `Conformance.aggregateNullSkipLaws`, filed by Phase 203): the package has a model now — `proofs/WireColumn.fst`, the columnar codec at the `JVal`, with the codec's image proved inside what `Table.validate` accepts and the round trip proved up to a normal form — which is the theorem that entry said an operator who wanted the codec proved would ask for by deleting it. What the entry cited is unchanged and is NOT what the model is about: `Column.aggregate` is still held by `aggregateNullSkipLaws` and, since the same phase, by a bit-for-bit differential against the fold it replaced; `DecimalText`'s arithmetic, `Schema.*` and the lenient-ingest arms of the decoder are not modelled, and the model's header says so.

operationClasses.trivial: The operation constructs, projects or looks up a value and computes nothing a law could be wrong about: a record builder, an accessor, a `List.tryFind` over declared data. The entry says what it does in one line so a reader can disagree.
operationClasses.forward: The operation delegates to ONE other public operation, adding only a default argument, a renamed spelling or a sentence rendering. It names that operation in `forwardsTo`, which must itself be mapped, so a forward's coverage is its target's and a forward to nothing is refused.
operationClasses.obsolete: The operation carries `System.Obsolete` and forwards to its replacement, which it names in `forwardsTo`. The clause reads the attribute by reflection, so an entry for an operation that is NOT marked obsolete is refused.
operationClasses.host-seam: The operation is a boundary whose content a host supplies: an interface member, a tool's entry point, an export another language's host diffs. What Core owns at that boundary is certified where the host meets it.
operationClasses.measured-elsewhere: The operation has behaviour and no theorem or law family states its contract; tests stand in. The entry names the test file in `standIn`, and the clause holds that file to mentioning the operation (`<Owner>.<member>`) or the `through` token naming the measured operation it is reached by, so a stand-in cannot point at a file that never touches it.

$operationsComment: Phase 335. The OPERATION clause of `Proofs.Coverage`: every public method or function in the committed API baselines (`../api/*.txt`, the `method` lines) maps to at least one of a `../proofs.json` row whose `evidence.operations` names it, a law family whose operation roster (`Fuaran.Core.Families.operations`) lists it, or an entry below with a class from `operationClasses` and a one-line reason. A law family's own entry point is mapped by its roster row. An operation is spelled `<Owner>.<member>` with the `Fuaran.Core.` prefix, generic arity and the compiler's `Module` suffix dropped and nested types joined by `.` (`Dag+ReachModule.ancestors` is `Dag.Reach.ancestors`). The baselines are the census, so a newly published operation reds the suite at the commit that adds it and names itself. The check runs both ways: an entry for an operation that is no longer published, or that has since gained a ladder row or a roster line, fails, as a member listed twice does. An entry is a recorded decision, not a pass: `measured-elsewhere` says no law states the contract, which is weaker than a theorem and says so.
